groups.title: Luggage Storage

about.title: A one-stop shop for everything cruise, open since 2016
text: We opened our doors in December 2016, in historic downtown Galveston, Texas. We are a one-stop shop for everything cruise.

Cruise guests who forgot something will find us a few minutes' walk from the Galveston cruise terminals, with sunscreen, motion-sickness aids, toiletries, cruise luggage tags, travel accessories and phone chargers. Ship crew drop by for ship-life essentials like toiletries, drinks and snacks, phone accessories, and small gifts and souvenirs to bring to loved ones.

We babysit bags, too. For those with late flights, shuttle pickups, or late check-ins for hotels and Airbnb, leave your bags with us and explore the island. And yes, we book Galveston cruises: call 409 739 6441 or visit thecruisestoptravel.com for details.
Thank you for visiting our store.

faqs.q: Where is the luggage storage place located?
faqs.a: The Cruise Stop is at 2002 Strand St Suite 101, Galveston Texas 77550.

faqs.q: Is it close to the cruise terminals? Can we walk from the terminal to the store?
faqs.a: We are within walking distance, less than a mile, of all four Galveston cruise terminals. With heavy luggage it is best to take an Uber, Lyft or taxi from the terminal; it takes about 2 to 5 minutes by car depending on which terminal you are coming from. On foot it is 0.5 miles and about 11 minutes from Terminal 25, 0.6 miles and 14 minutes from Terminal 28, 0.5 miles and 12 minutes from Terminal 16, and 0.7 miles and 16 minutes from Terminal 10. Stay safe and always use the crosswalk and the sidewalk.
Just $6 per bag, per piece, any size, with a reservation. Walk-ins with no reservation are charged $7 per bag.

faqs.q: Do backpacks, tote bags, plastic bags, paper bags or car seats count?
faqs.a: Yes. Each bag or car seat is counted as a separate piece and costs $6 regardless of size or material. Any bag stacked on top of or attached in any way to another bag is counted as a separate piece.

faqs.q: What are the storage hours? What time is the latest for pickup?
faqs.a: Storage hours are from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm.

Yes. Space is limited, so do make a reservation at the-cruise-stop.booqable.store. You will not be required to prepay and you can cancel anytime. Payment will be collected at the location on the day of service.

faqs.q: How do I cancel my reservation if plans change?
faqs.a: Just call 409 497 2974 or send an email to cs@thecruisestoponline.com.

faqs.q: Where are the bags stored? Is it air-conditioned?
faqs.a: Your bags will be stored in the store's storage rooms, which are air-conditioned. Only staff has access to the storage area.

faqs.q: Is the store close to downtown and tourist attractions?
faqs.a: The Cruise Stop is on the Strand in downtown Galveston, just steps away from restaurants, shops, art galleries and tourist attractions.

faqs.q: Can I store a bag for multiple days?
faqs.a: Maybe, if there is nothing fragile, perishable or smelly in your bag, and no weapons or anything illegal. Please call 409 497 2974 to ask.

faqs.q: Anything else I need to know?
faqs.a: There is no restroom in the store. Make sure you use the restroom where you are coming from before dropping off or picking up your bags.

facts.heading: Which terminal your ship uses
items: Carnival, Princess and Disney use both Terminal 25 and Terminal 28, which sit next to each other, so you can walk over if you are dropped at the wrong one
Royal Caribbean sails from Terminal 10, and its Oasis class ships such as Allure, Harmony and Symphony dock there
MSC Cruises and Norwegian Cruise Line sail from Terminal 16
When a line has two ships in port, the bigger one is at that line's main terminal and the smaller one is most likely at Terminal 28
Carnival's Excel class ships, such as the Carnival Jubilee, are at Terminal 25

facts.heading: About the four terminals
items: Terminal 25, once called Cruise Terminal 1, is closest to the downtown shops and restaurants, and is home to the Carnival Jubilee, the made-for-Texas Excel class ship that holds 6,600 passengers
Terminal 28, once called Cruise Terminal 2, is a plain building with x-ray machines inside

Terminal 10, the Royal Caribbean terminal, is the nicest so far but furthest from downtown, with the giant propellers hanging from the ceiling, the Galveston Beach Trio sculpture and a much nicer waiting area than the older terminals
Terminal 16, the MSC terminal, opened in November 2025
The elevated pedestrian walkway over Harborside Drive at Terminal 25 is not in operation and has been closed for decades, so use the crosswalk at street level
